subject: MSA/Addendum: defining operator footprint & audit runbook for VPC deployment
messages:
From: Sophie Park <sophie.park@clinixlabs.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops (Clinix Labs) <legal@clinixlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA/Addendum: operator access & audit runbook for VPC deployment

Neha —

Thanks for the product demo yesterday. Clinix Labs is excited to move forward with a private VPC deployment for our production environment, but legal and procurement flagged a few items that must be clarified in the MSA/Addendum before we proceed:

- Precise definition of "operator access" (who, when, scope).
- Audit evidence we can request in a post-go-live window (for SOC-like reads and snapshots).
- Temporary access windows for incident response and how they are invoked.
- Whether we need an escrow-like mechanism for runtime artifacts or a witness model.

Can you share your proposed language for an addendum and an outline of the operational runbook that your team would follow during audits? Our legal team would like enough specificity to sign off on the license boundary and evidence requests.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement has a vendor approval cut-off next week.

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Park
Head of IT Security, Clinix Labs
---
Attachment: none in this message

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Park <sophie.park@clinixlabs.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA/Addendum: operator access & audit runbook for VPC deployment

Sophie —

Thanks for laying this out. I attached a draft addendum and a one-pager runbook outline to start the conversation. High level summary here:

- Operator access scope: Redwood will define "operator" as named Redwood personnel with documented role-based privileges; access is time-boxed and logged to the customer's audit channel. We propose two classes: emergency break-glass (invoked by customer auth) and scheduled maintenance (pre-approved windows).
- Evidence & snapshots: We can provide time-limited forensic snapshots and signed attestations of actions taken during an access window. We cannot provide live access to system internals outside of the mechanisms described.
- Escrow vs witness: Redwood prefers a witness-based model for most customers (witnessed snapshot + attestation) rather than depositing runtime artifacts into escrow. However, we can discuss limited escrow/escrow-lite for regulated customers with additional contracting.
- Order form linkage: we'll add an exhibit to the order form that maps the deployment tier to permitted access levels and audit frequency.

Next steps I propose: 1) Legal redline to the attached draft addendum, 2) A short walkthrough call with David (runtime/auth) and Ben (sales/orderform) to align on evidence mechanics, 3) Procurement timeline from Tom at ProcureCorp.

I've attached: 1) 20261027-Redwood-Clinix-VPC-Addendum-draft.docx (draft language), 2) operator-runbook-outline.pdf (runbook one-pager).

Available for a 30-minute call tomorrow 10/28 between 10–11am PT. Would that work?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Attachment: 20261027-Redwood-Clinix-VPC-Addendum-draft.docx (DOCX), operator-runbook-outline.pdf (PDF)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA/Addendum: operator access & audit runbook for VPC deployment

Sophie / Neha —

Quick technical notes after reviewing Neha's draft:

1) Operator identity & authentication: we must be explicit that operator sessions are authenticated via Redwood SSO + MFA and that we log both session metadata and any KV-cache purge/rollback actions. Suggest adding a clause: "Redwood will provide a signed session log within 72 hours of a formal evidence request."

2) Access windows & escalation: for emergency break-glass we need a customer-designated approver list (name + contact) in the order form. We can automate a 15-minute notification window before break-glass if desired.

3) Evidence artifacts & retention: Redwood retains short-term forensic artifacts for 30 days by default; extending retention is possible as an add-on but must be priced in the order form. Suggest adding an exhibit that describes evidence artifacts (signed snapshot, audit log export, runbook execution transcript).

4) Witness vs escrow: the witness model works operationally; escrow introduces complexity (build artifact custody, rebuild testing). If Clinix requires escrow, we should scope a limited "sealed snapshot deposit" focused only on runtime image and provenance metadata rather than full secrets or keys.

I'll be on the call tomorrow if we confirm. I'll attach a compact evidence checklist (evidence-checklist.xlsx) to help legal map items.

-David
David Kim
Director, Runtime & Reliability, Redwood Inference
Attachment: evidence-checklist.xlsx (XLSX)

Team —

Thanks for the clarity. A couple of procurement asks from our side before we green-light legal to sign:

- Please confirm the SLA carve-out if we invoke emergency operator access (we need a maximum time to termination of any live operator session).
- We will require a short onboarding attestation for our internal auditors confirming the witness model and the deliverables we will receive during an audit.
- If you propose an escrow-lite, please provide a short statement of custody (what gets deposited, under whose custody, and the access gating).

If you can put the SLA carve-out language and the short onboarding attestation into the addendum (even as examples) that will speed procurement. Our legal team is available for a 30-minute redline session Monday the 1st.

Regards,
Tom Reynolds
Senior Procurement Manager, ProcureCorp (on behalf of Clinix Labs)
